## The short list

| Tool | What it is | Get it |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub account | Hosts the repository; required for Codespaces and Copilot | <https://github.com/signup> |
| Git | Version control on your machine | <https://git-scm.com/downloads> |
| R | The language the pipeline runs in | <https://cloud.r-project.org> |
| RStudio Desktop | IDE for R; has a Git tab and Copilot support | <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/> |
| VS Code | IDE used for Copilot and the Claude Code extension | <https://code.visualstudio.com/download> |
| Quarto | Renders this book and the slides | <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/> |
| Node.js (LTS) | Only needed to install Claude Code via `npm` | <https://nodejs.org/en/download> |

::: {.note}
[Install R before RStudio]{.note-head}
RStudio is an interface to R, not a copy of it. Install R first, then RStudio, then
reopen RStudio so it finds the installation.
:::

## Platform notes

**macOS.** Git ships with the Command Line Tools: run `xcode-select --install` in
Terminal. For R, download the `.pkg` for your chip (Apple silicon vs. Intel) from
CRAN. [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) is a convenient alternative for everything here
(`brew install git node quarto`, `brew install --cask r rstudio visual-studio-code`).

**Windows.** Install [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) and accept
the defaults; it provides Git Bash, which is where the commands in these chapters
work as written. R and RStudio are both ordinary installers. If `git` is not found
afterwards, close and reopen the terminal.

**Linux.** `sudo apt install git` (or your package manager's equivalent);
[CRAN has per-distribution instructions](https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/) for R.

## Verify the install

Open a terminal — in RStudio, **Tools → Terminal → New Terminal** — and run:

```bash
git --version
R --version
quarto --version
node --version      # only if you plan to install Claude Code with npm
```

Each should print a version number. Anything that prints "command not found" is not
installed, or is not on your `PATH`; reopening the terminal fixes the second case
most of the time.

Then identify yourself to Git, once per machine:

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@unm.edu"
```

## The AI tools

**GitHub Copilot.** Free tier for everyone; students and faculty get Copilot Pro
through [GitHub Education](https://education.github.com). In VS Code, install the
**GitHub Copilot** and **GitHub Copilot Chat** extensions and sign in. In RStudio,
**Tools → Global Options → Copilot → Enable**.

**Claude Code.** Requires a Claude Pro/Max subscription or an API key.

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code    # or: brew install claude-code
cd UNM_Workshop
claude
```

There is also a **Claude Code** extension in the VS Code marketplace, which is the
same tool with a panel instead of a terminal.

**GitHub CLI** (optional, but it makes authentication painless):
[cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com), then `gh auth login` and `gh auth status`.

## Zero-install options {#zero-install-options}

| Option | What you need | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| [GitHub Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/crweber9874/UNM_Workshop) | GitHub account | The full environment — R, tidyverse, RStudio Server on port 8787, Quarto, Copilot, Claude Code — in a browser tab |
| [Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud) | Free account | RStudio in the browser; clone the repo from its terminal. No Claude Code |
| [Download the ZIP](https://github.com/crweber9874/UNM_Workshop/archive/refs/heads/main.zip) | Nothing | Reading the code and data without Git |
| This site | Nothing | Every chapter shows its code and output; the slides are [here](slides/workshop.qmd) |

::: {.warn}
[If you use a Codespace]{.warn-head}
The free tier is 60 core-hours a month and it bills while it idles. **Stop the
codespace when you are done** — Code → Codespaces → ⋯ → Stop codespace.
:::

::: {.note}
[The ZIP is not a clone]{.note-head}
A ZIP download has no `.git` directory, so there is no history, no `git diff`, and no
way to undo an agent's edits. Fine for reading; not the setup to let an agent work in.
:::

## Then what

Clone the repository and check that it runs:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/crweber9874/UNM_Workshop.git
cd UNM_Workshop
Rscript R/01_recode.R
```

Missing packages are the usual first error. Install what the pipeline needs:

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "haven", "survey", "broom",
                   "here", "scales", "testthat", "shiny"))
```

The Bayesian section of [the analysis chapter](08-analysis.qmd) uses `brms`, which
compiles Stan models and takes considerably longer to install. Add it only if you
intend to run that part:

```r
install.packages("brms")
```

From there, continue to [Setup](02-setup.qmd).
